Serializing the entire `input` object using `JSON.stringify(_exhaustive)` can lead to sensitive user data (such as `situation`, `dilemma`, or `apology`) being leaked into application logs or error monitoring systems (e.g., Sentry). Since the compile-time exhaustiveness check is already guaranteed by `const _exhaustive: never = input;`, we only need to extract and throw the invalid `toolId` at runtime. We can safely do this by casting `input` directly without a double-cast.

```suggestion
			throw new Error(`Unknown toolId: ${(input as { toolId?: string }).toolId}`);
```
